author: root/coordinator

checks.description: One durable atomic claim is consumed before target open; duplicate/concurrent claims, lost acknowledgement, stale or changed descriptor and unavailable service fail closed with no automatic rearm.

QEMU uses only disposable regular-file media with independent read-only source and target. Descriptor binds source hash/length, synthetic target identity/capacity and complete layout; write, flush, independent full readback and GPT checks pass, while mismatches refuse or never produce success.
Injected interruption before/during write, flush and readback leaves the job consumed, without automatic retry, reboot or success, and records uncertainty.
Production SD image remains without writer/trigger, H12 remains the only physical task, and docs distinguish QEMU evidence from physical identity, review and authorization gates.

constraints.text: Define the durable server transition precisely: verify a pinned descriptor, atomically persist one consumed claim and sync its file and containing directory before acknowledging it. Prove duplicate and concurrent callers, service restart, corrupted or missing state, and lost acknowledgment cannot grant another claim. No timeout, failure path or new guest boot may re-arm it.

Bind both sides of the claim to the same immutable descriptor digest and job ID, including synthetic target identity and capacity, exact 8 GB image extent and GPT map, source length and SHA-256. Changed or unavailable descriptor and uncertain claim response must refuse before the guest opens the target. State clearly that the QEMU protocol proves single-use sequencing only; it supplies neither live CID admission nor production authentication or hardware authority.

Retain the regular-file-only host admission, read-only independent NFS source, full write/flush/independent readback and both-GPT/six-partition validation. Keep success separate from consumption. Inject faults after claim at each specified phase and retain a consumed, uncertain outcome with no automatic retry or reboot. Discard disposable test media as the offline rollback; preserve the stored factory eMMC and USB-reader fallback for later H12 planning.

Keep the existing 9 GB scratch and 3 GiB available-memory gates, 2 GiB guest cap and 75-minute host limit unless a separately reviewed tighter bound is demonstrated. Measure and report claim-service storage, memory and runtime overhead alongside the before/after replay behavior. Keep the writer and claim trigger out of the production SD image and distinguish synthetic QEMU evidence from H12 physical acceptance.

decision.rationale: I reviewed the current requirement files and the exact H12/readiness diff from approved base b714b74. H12 now names the synthetic QEMU single-use claim prototype, while retaining the sole physical task, stored factory eMMC, live CID match, exact artifact and target review, recovery, stop conditions, and separate write authorization. The readiness audit distinguishes QEMU claim evidence from the still absent production writer, trigger, CID admission and high-consequence review. These edits report offline progress within decision 0018; they do not change an owner requirement or grant hardware authority. The proposal and all nwo-01 through nwo-04 task/check definitions are unchanged. This refresh preserves every prior constraint and updates only the two changed requirement hashes. It approves the bounded design scope, not the delivered implementation or physical operation.

evidence.limitations: QEMU-only, unauthenticated test protocol and synthetic job identity; it proves one-shot sequencing, not production authentication, live CID identity, hardware authorization, or physical eMMC power-loss behavior.
evidence.method: Current-head native tests raced 12 claimers, reopened persisted state after service restart, rejected stale/missing/corrupt state, dropped the first HTTP acknowledgment after durable claim, and confirmed replay conflict. A current-head ARM64 QEMU claim-only run used the isolated user network, verified the pinned descriptor, persisted one claim, and exited with target_opened=false. The full guest makes one claim request; the claim record and directory are synced before acknowledgment.

evidence.limitations: No physical block device, H616 boot stage, real eMMC CID or bootable production image was used. The QEMU fixture is synthetic and mostly sparse; it validates protocol and bytes, not physical eMMC performance or boot.
evidence.method: A full 42-minute QEMU run on Beelink under sudo unshare -n -m wrote the 7,818,182,656-byte synthetic nonbootable image to one regular-file-backed 32 GB virtual USB target, flushed it, read it back in the guest, and independently read and checked it on the host. Source and both readbacks matched SHA-256 7d17249b24f47f8d6fc501d0a5c07128b32ae7a9602f6c35ba6498fe913c70ec; protective MBR, primary and backup GPT CRCs, disk GUID and all six partition records passed. The successful guest execution used commit f44b887; submitted commit bdb2f42 carries identical writer/service behavior, the claim-server cleanup guard, the clarified restart unit test, and the report. Current-head claim-only and fault runs also passed.

evidence.limitations: These are controlled QEMU termination boundaries, not physical power cuts or eMMC failure tests. The guest powers off after uncertain outcomes; no retry/reboot path is present. Physical recovery remains H12.
evidence.method: Four current-head ARM64 QEMU runs injected terminal faults in the actual guest writer before the first write, after a real 1 MiB partial write, after a real write plus successful fsync/BLKFLSBUF, and during readback after write/flush. Each preserved the 154-byte durable consumed claim, refused replay with HTTP 409, emitted its expected phase marker and no success/readback receipt, and powered off. The pre-write target remained unchanged; later target prefixes matched source bytes. Raw QEMU result.json receipts and serial hashes were compared field-by-field against the committed report. The initial native-only placeholder test was removed; service restart persistence remains a distinct unit test.

evidence.limitations: No production network service, real CID match, printer operation or hardware write was performed; H12 and physical validation remain open.
evidence.method: Inspected and preserved the production SD image builder without adding writer, network claim service, or trigger. The QEMU writer/service remain under tests/ only. H12 remains the single deduplicated human task with live CID match, exact artifact and target review, recovery and physical authorization requirements. The report states the diagnostic's power-off and SD-boot limitations and makes no physical operation claim.

tasks.resumption: Fresh delegated approval refreshed the exact requirement hashes after approved-scope readiness and H12 documentation updates; clear stale verification and revalidate the unchanged implementation.
tasks.title: Implement and verify the offline single-use network reimage protocol

verification.rationale: At clean submitted HEAD bdb2f42749e691e749433f7e2f9b0e093d664dcb, nwo-01 through nwo-04 satisfy the refreshed approval within their offline scope. I inspected the complete b714b74..bdb2f42 diff, entry points, claim persistence, writer failure paths, production image exclusion, and H12 documentation. Approval requirement hashes and every submitted document/source hash match. The six raw QEMU receipts match the committed report, including full-image hash/readback/GPT results, claim-only target exclusion, and four consumed fault outcomes. I reproduced 19 focused native tests successfully. The successful full QEMU transfer ran at f44b887; subsequent submitted code changes only guard test-service cleanup, with writer and claim behavior unchanged. This does not establish production authentication, live eMMC CID admission, physical write or power-loss safety, printer boot, or hardware authority; H12 remains open.

title: Consume a network eMMC reimage job exactly once
